title: Inbound SLA-aware feature routing for hosted API requests (chat/streaming/tool-calls/structured outputs)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a repeatable intake and routing system for hosted-API feature requests from enterprise customers that automatically tags and escalates high-SLA-impact requests across chat, streaming, tool/function-calling, and structured output workstreams. Goal: reduce TOA (time-to-assess) to < 24h for SLA-impacting requests and ensure appropriate engineering, solutions, and legal handoffs are triggered consistently.
background: Over the last 6 months we've seen increased enterprise asks that cut across multiple capabilities: streaming reliability for long-lived calls, stricter structured-output schemas, function/tool calling guarantees, and SLO-sensitive latency requirements. Current intake is ad-hoc via email and CSM notes; this causes slow assessments and missed SLAs for customers on contracts. Existing artifacts: intake playbooks (PM-7382), enterprise priority matrices (PM-9157), and routing experiments (PM-21456). This ticket consolidates into a production routing + SLA tagging flow.
acceptance_criteria: An updated intake form (Console + intake form template) that collects key signals: customer tier, contract SLA, traffic estimate, model types, expected latency/throughput, security constraints, and whether request touches PII or restricted data
Automated scoring engine (rule-based) that assigns an initial priority bucket: "SLA-critical", "High enterprise", "Standard"

Routing rules implemented in the intake pipeline that: (a) create Linear ticket with PM/AE tags, (b) notify on-call solutions-engineer Slack channel for "SLA-critical" items, (c) attach expected response SLA (24h/72h) based on bucket
UI visibility in Console intake dashboard showing queue, signals, and historical time-to-assess metrics
Playbook doc for PMs/CSMs that maps scoring outputs to next-step templates (e.g., kickoff, architecture spike, contract review, POC request)
At least one pilot with an existing enterprise customer, and measured TOA < 24h for SLA-critical pilot tickets
out_of_scope: Changes to runtime implementation (kernel/serving) or Dedicated capacity provisioning are out of scope for the intake routing automation; those are handled by downstream engineering tickets after triage.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement intake form + rules and run a 2-week pilot with 2 customers. Phase 2: incorporate feedback, add Console dashboard, and extend to self-serve intake forms for non-enterprise. Phase 3: bake into sales onboarding and AE playbooks.
implementation_steps: Design revised intake schema (fields + examples) with Solutions Eng and CSM
Implement intake form in Console and webhook to intake pipeline
Add rule engine that computes scoring and writes tags/fields to Linear ticket
Create Slack automation + on-call routing for SLA-critical bucket
Build Console dashboard for intake queue and metrics
Run pilot, collect metrics, and iterate
updates: 2025-11-04 - Created: initial problem statement and goal. Assigned to Luca for kickoff.
2025-11-06 - Sync: Met with Solutions Eng (Ravi) and CSM leads. Agreed on minimal required fields and 24h TOA SLAs for SLA-critical.
2025-11-08 - Decision: Use rule-based scoring for MVP instead of ML because rules are interpretable for legal/CSMs.
2025-11-10 - Engineering spike: ENG-32812 scoped a webhook and Linear ticket creator service. Estimated 4 points for backend work.
2025-11-12 - Security: Sent intake schema to Security for review; flagged PII field handling and KMS requirements. Security review required before pilot launch.
notes: We should avoid over-optimizing the scoring rubric; keep it transparent and allow manual overrides by PM/AE. For structured-output requests, include an optional sample schema upload to speed engineering assessment.
next_steps: Finalize intake fields, draft Console form UX, schedule implementation kickoff with ENG and SE, and prep pilot customer list.
